Extract latent coordinates and loadings from an rrGDM model

Source: R/get_LV.R
get_LV.Rd

Extracts the main components of the fitted latent space of an rrGDM object as a list of matrices (see also biplot.rrGDM).

Usage

get_LV(object, rotate = TRUE)

Arguments

object

A fitted model of class rrGDM.

rotate

Logical indicating whether to apply varimax rotation (via varimax) before returning the results. Default is TRUE. The rotation is estimated from the conditional coordinates (L).

Value

A list of matrices, with latent dimensions (LV1, LV2, ...) as columns:

  • lambda: environmental loadings (predictors x latent dimensions).

  • u_sample: sample-level errors (samples x latent dimensions).

  • u_re: additional random effects, e.g. (1 | group) (groups x latent dimensions). Omitted if the model has none.

  • L: conditional coordinates of the samples (samples x latent dimensions).

  • L_m: marginal coordinates of the samples (samples x latent dimensions).

  • rotation: the rotation matrix applied (the identity matrix if rotate = FALSE), useful to rotate other quantities consistently.

Details

Latent positions of the samples are built as L_m = X %*% lambda (marginal: determined by the predictors only) and L = L_m + u_sample (+ Z %*% u_re) (conditional: also including sample-level errors and any other random effects). Rotating all matrices with the same rotation matrix preserves these relationships and all pairwise distances between samples.

Examples

set.seed(1)
# Simulate data
n <- 50 # sites
p <- 25 # species
env <- data.frame(temp = rnorm(n), moist = rnorm(n))
eta <- as.matrix(env) %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * p), 2, p)
Y <- matrix(rpois(n * p, exp(1 + 0.8 * eta)), n, p,
            dimnames = list(paste0("site", 1:n), paste0("sp", 1:p)))

fit <- rrGDM(Y, env, k = 2, formula = ~ temp + moist,
             family = "binomial")
#> ℹ Preparing data
#> ✔ Preparing data ... done
#> 
#> ℹ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA)
#> ✔ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA) ... done
#> 
#> ℹ optimisation
#> ℹ Start 1/1: objective = 6152.6868
#> ℹ optimisation

#> ✔ optimisation ... done
#> 

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # basic biplot
  biplot(fit)
  # add species correlations with latent variables
  biplot(fit, type = "marginal", species_cor = TRUE)
  # colour by predictor
  biplot(fit, col_by = "moist") + ggplot2::scale_colour_viridis_c()
}
#> ℹ Labelling only the 20 species with the strongest correlation (25 available).
#> • Increase `species_cor_n`, or set it to `NULL`, to label more.
